title: “IF YOU REALLY MEAN IT…”
paragraphs: “IF YOU REALLY MEAN IT…”
That was Gideon’s prayer.

Not polished.
Not heroic.
Not the kind you frame on a wall.
It sounded more like this:
“Lord… if You really mean what You said… prove it.”
And heaven did not strike him down for asking.
Israel was crushed under Midian’s boot in Judges 6.

Crops stolen.
Families hiding in caves.
Hope… buried in the dust.
And Gideon?
He wasn’t standing tall with a sword.
He was hiding in a winepress, secretly threshing wheat so the enemy wouldn’t see.
Fear was his shadow.
Then the Angel of the LORD appeared and spoke words that sounded almost ridiculous:
“The LORD is with you, mighty warrior.”
Mighty?
The man was shaking in a pit.
Here is the tension most people miss.
Gideon believed.
But his faith trembled.
So he said the words many believers are too ashamed to say out loud:

“If You will save Israel by my hand as You have said… show me a sign.”
(Judges 6:36)
Not rebellion.
Just a heart trying to trust while fear whispered.
So Gideon laid a fleece on the ground.
First test:

Dew on the fleece.
Dry ground everywhere else.
Morning came.
The fleece was soaked. Gideon wrung out a bowl full of water.
But Gideon still trembled.
So he asked again:
“Lord… don’t be angry… just one more.”
Second test:

Dry fleece.
Wet ground.
And God answered again.
Here’s the beautiful scandal of grace.
God did not reject Gideon for his trembling faith.
He met him inside it.
Because the story of Gideon is not about a confident hero.
It’s about a patient God.
A God who turns fearful farmers into deliverers.
A God who walks gently with people who believe… but still shake.
But here is the deeper truth.
The greatest sign was still coming.
Not a fleece.
A cross.
At the cross, God didn’t just prove His plan.
He proved His love.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Jesus is the ultimate answer to every trembling prayer that begins with:
“Lord… if You really mean it…”
The empty tomb shouts back:
“I meant it all along.”
So if your faith feels small today…
If fear is whispering louder than courage…
If you are quietly asking God for reassurance—
You are standing exactly where Gideon once stood.
And the same God is still speaking.
Not with anger.
But with invitation.

Trust Me.
Walk with Me.
I will finish what I started.
Because many people don’t need stronger faith.
They just need to know God is patient with trembling hearts.
